beats: Hook: classical bits can only flip; qubits can also flip a sign no classical code had ever heard of (line_qc_shor_unseen_trick: the keeper in round glasses sees two dark bulbs while the imp, in square glasses, tiptoes off). Peter Shor's 1995 fix: nine qubits, two layers (line_qc_shor_three_floors). Cast as in QC08-01: the keeper (the code) and the imp (the noise). The glasses are QC05-02's two lenses (reuse line_qc_hbridge_two_glasses): round = the 0/1 (Z) lens, square = the +/- (X) lens; the imp in square glasses is a phase flip, an ordinary flip seen through the other lens.
Roadmap (50:32-51:24): X, then Z, then both, then everything (pen work; reuse line_qc_vote_switch_fix for the X step already done).

Z is a bit flip in the +/- basis (51:50-52:44; clip 52:15-52:44; tape Q24-09 p15): reuse line_qc_phase_coin_turn (edge-on the two look alike; turned, the difference shows); line_qc_shor_glasses_catch: the keeper puts on the square glasses and the imp's trick is an ordinary flip.

The |+++>, |---> code (52:44-56:55): the bit-flip encoder followed by Hadamards, change the lens, act, change back (reuse line_qc_hbridge_cake_turntable); its checks are X-type, X1X2 and X2X3, read through the square lens (line_qc_shor_glasses_catch); syndromes and fixes (56:55-59:49).

Shor's code by concatenation (59:51-62:03; clip 59:51-60:16; tape Q24-09 p19): the phase code outside, the bit-flip code inside; 8 checks (62:03-64:00): each floor's two small bulbs are the six Z-type checks inside one block of three, and the two big lanterns between floors are the two X-type checks comparing neighbouring blocks (line_qc_shor_three_floors: 9 covered plates, 6 small bulbs, 2 lanterns).

Counting (64:36-67:15): 27 single-qubit errors (9 qubits x X, Y, Z) against 2^8 = 256 syndromes; some two-qubit errors are fixable too, but not all of them (C(9,2) x 9 = 324 > 256) (reuse line_card_catalog: a wall of drawers, few in use).

Quiz (67:28-69:41; tape Q24-09 p21): an XZ error on qubit 4 (line_qc_shor_quiz_floors: the middle floor's left bulb and both lanterns lit; pause, then the answer: flip the sign of block 2 and flip qubit 4 back).

Degenerate, but not a problem (Q25-11 06:23-10:02, clip 07:43-08:10; Q24-09 65:00-68:32): a phase flip on any one of a block's three qubits gives the very same state, so different errors share a syndrome and the same fix works whichever it was (line_qc_shor_tablecloth_tug: a tug at any seat slides the whole cloth; the keeper straightens it from her own seat). Cite Shor, PRA 52, R2493 (1995) by name only; no portrait.
Cover (line_qc_cover_08_03; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the keeper, in square glasses, catches the imp in square glasses red-handed beside a covered plate.
